name: Metaphor worlds
purpose: abstract ideas made concrete through one real place: hidden risk, safe passage and trust, building toward each other, systems and dependencies, growth over time, long journeys and milestones

identity.place: A fictional fishing harbour town of about 600 people on a granite headland on a cold North Atlantic coast, in late May, when icebergs drift south past the coast. The town sits around a small sheltered harbour that opens to the east; a white lighthouse stands on the headland south of the harbour mouth, with its keeper's house and a walled kitchen garden in the lee of the tower; behind the town a footpath climbs a bare hill to a summit cairn; across the narrow inlet north of the town a new concrete road bridge is being built from both banks. Every set is a spot in this one place, so the same lighthouse, the same granite and the same sea recur. No real town is drawn.
architecture: two-storey timber houses with steep gable roofs and narrow clapboard siding, painted in a few muted colours (ochre, oxblood red, slate blue, off-white) with white window trims and six-pane sash windows, standing on low granite footings and stepping up the slope; no shop signs or names

the harbour: a straight quay of squared granite blocks with a concrete capping, black cast-iron bollards about 5 m apart and 0.5 m back from the edge, vertical timber fenders on the quay face, a steel ladder recessed into the wall; a curved rubble breakwater of big granite blocks across the south side of the harbour mouth, with a short white light tower with a red lantern on its head, and a small green light on a white post at the quay's end
single-storey fishing stores along the quay: timber sheds with pitched roofs of dark grey corrugated sheet, wide double doors, weathered silver-grey boards

the lighthouse: a round tapering tower of white-painted masonry about 18 m tall on the headland's highest rock, a black-painted iron gallery with railings, a glazed lantern with diagonal glazing bars and a red-painted domed roof with a ball vent; inside, below the lantern, a round watch room holds the weight-driven clockwork that still turns the lens; the station is kept as a working heritage light, wound by hand by a part-time keeper
the land: bare grey-pink granite in rounded outcrops and cliffs, low wind-shaped spruce in the hollows, crowberry and grass heath, small dark ponds; no tall trees

the new bridge: a concrete box-girder road bridge built by the balanced cantilever method, two slim piers in the inlet, each carrying a deck that grows outward both ways in 5 m segments, with yellow form travellers at the tips of the growing deck and a tower crane beside each pier
identity.materials: grey-pink granite, painted clapboard (muted ochre, oxblood, slate blue, off-white), silver-grey weathered timber, black cast iron and painted steel, white-painted masonry, fresh pale-grey concrete, rope and netting, a deep blue-green sea and white-and-pale-blue ice; signal red and orange only on things that carry them in life (the lantern roof, the breakwater light, lifebuoys, fishing floats, a rescue boat's collar), and warning yellow only on the bridge's construction plant (the cranes, the form travellers). Palette families in this outdoor world (the set palette was named for rooms): the sky is sky; the sea and other water are glass (its deep tone for deep water, its highlight for glints); ice is paper, its shaded faces glass; granite, rock and distant land are exterior; grass, heath and spruce are plant; the quay top, paths and soil are floor; concrete is wall; painted clapboard is wall2 or fabric2; timber is wood; iron and steel are metal; brass is brass; the few red or orange things are accent
inhabited: work everywhere: lobster pots stacked on the quay, coiled ropes, plastic fish tubs, a hose, gloves drying on a bollard
domestic life: laundry on a line behind a house, a woodpile under a lean-to, a bicycle against a shed, a kettle-black chimney smoking thinly
care and wear: paint flaking on the stores, rust streaks under the bollards, seaweed on the lower quay stones, patched netting

safety things where they really are: lifebuoys on boards on the store walls, a ladder in the quay face, handrails on the lighthouse gallery, site fencing and hard-hat signs (pictograms only) at the bridge
scale: a person is about 1.75 m tall; a house door is about 2.0 m high; a house ridge about 8 m above the ground
the quay top stands about 2.5 m above the water at mid tide; a bollard is about 0.5 m tall; a lobster pot is about 0.9 by 0.6 by 0.45 m
the lighthouse tower is about 18 m tall to the gallery plus a 4 m lantern, on rock about 20 m above the sea; the watch room inside is about 4.2 m across and 2.7 m high
a small fishing boat is 10 to 12 m long with a wheelhouse about 2.5 m tall
the icebergs offshore are medium icebergs: about 30 to 40 m above the water and about 100 m long, with about nine tenths of the ice under water
the bridge's main span is 120 m between two piers; its deck top is about 22 m above the water; each cast segment is about 5 m long; the tower cranes stand about 45 m tall
identity.default_light: Late May, a clear cold afternoon: the sun about 40 degrees high in the south-west, crisp shadows tinted cool blue, the sea deep blue-green and darker toward the horizon, thin high cloud; white surfaces (the lighthouse, the ice) bright but never pure white, their shaded sides pale blue.
identity.motifs: Use at least three of these in every outdoor scene so the sets belong to one place (each scene names the ones its camera can see): the white lighthouse with its red lantern roof, grey-pink granite, painted clapboard houses, a white iceberg on the sea, black iron bollards or railings, stacked lobster pots and coiled rope, the deep blue-green sea.
avoid: real towns, real lighthouses, flags, names on boats or buildings, signs with words, brands or logos
a tropical or Mediterranean look: palm trees, sandy beaches, terracotta roofs, turquoise water
a lighthouse with painted stripes, no gallery or a lantern without glazing bars
icebergs inside the harbour, or an iceberg drawn as a floating white triangle with nothing under the water
people in the sets (the cast is separate)
a cartoon-clean place: every set shows that people live and work here
objects at the wrong size: a person must fit through a door, a bollard reaches only to the knee
identity.outside: The sea to the east runs to a clear horizon; icebergs stand on it; to the west the land rises in bare granite hills; no other towns are visible.

cast.role: the lesson's cast at full scale, standing in the places of this one town (from the lesson's cast)
harbour people drawn with dignity: a harbour master, fishers, the part-time lighthouse keeper, a gardener
the bridge's site team in hard hats and high-visibility vests: a site engineer, a project manager
two walkers in outdoor clothes for the hill path: a guide and a newcomer
an original guide (C9) who can stand in any set
local creatures that belong here (C14): gulls, a puffin, a robin, a cat on the quay

core: iceberg (above and below water as groups)
lighthouse (lantern as a group, beam as a group)
bridge deck segment and form traveller
clockwork gears (each gear its own group with a pivot)
raised bed with plants at four stages

research: Real-place facts checked on 2026-10-13 to 15 (iceberg flotation, size classes and draft-to-height ratios, the iceberg season off cold North Atlantic coasts, lighthouse rotation clockwork and watch rooms, balanced cantilever bridge building, fishing harbour quay furniture, upland path and waymarker sizes, walled kitchen gardens, raised beds and cold frames). Sources and what was not verified: docs/research/2026-10-13-sets-metaphor.md.

objects.quay: a straight harbour wall of squared grey-pink granite blocks in level courses, each block about 1.2 m by 0.6 m, with a 0.3 m concrete capping along the top edge; the face drops vertically about 2.5 m to the water at mid tide, darker and green-brown with weed in its lowest metre; the top is a flat surface of worn concrete and old granite setts, with drainage gaps
objects.bollard: a black cast-iron mooring bollard about 0.5 m tall: a short thick column about 0.3 m across, slightly waisted, with a wider rounded cap that overhangs to stop a rope slipping off, bolted to the quay on a square base plate; rust streaks below it
objects.fender: vertical timber fenders on the quay face: squared timbers about 0.3 m wide, from the capping down to below the water, bolted on every few metres, rubbed pale where boats touch
objects.quay ladder: a steel ladder fixed into a vertical recess in the quay face so it does not stick out: two flat rails about 0.4 m apart, round rungs every 0.3 m, the rails curving over the capping as hand grips, running down into the water
objects.lobster pot: a rectangular trap about 0.9 by 0.6 by 0.45 m: a frame of bent steel rod or timber laths covered in green or yellow plastic-coated wire mesh, with a funnel entrance of netting on each side, a bricked weight in the base; stacked three or four high in neat rows, each with a coil of rope and a small orange float
objects.rope coil: a mooring rope about 3 cm thick laid in a flat round coil about 0.8 m across on the ground, its loops visible, one end trailing; blue or orange synthetic rope, faded
objects.fish tub: a heavy plastic fish tub about 0.9 by 0.6 by 0.45 m with rounded corners and moulded hand holds, in faded blue or grey, stacked in twos
objects.fishing store: a single-storey timber shed about 6 m wide and 8 m deep: weathered silver-grey vertical boards, a pitched roof of dark grey corrugated sheet with the ridge about 5 m up, a pair of wide doors facing the quay with iron strap hinges, one small four-pane window; nets and floats hung on nails by the door
objects.lifebuoy: a ring lifebuoy about 0.75 m across, orange with four white bands and a grab line looped around it, hung on a small painted board with a peg; the board fixed to a wall at about 1.5 m
objects.fishing boat: a small inshore fishing boat 10 to 12 m long: a white-painted hull with a raised bow, a dark red waterline band, a wheelhouse about 2.5 m tall set toward the bow with three front windows, an open working deck at the stern with a hauler and a short mast with a light; no name or number on the hull
objects.breakwater: a mound of big rough granite blocks (each 1 to 3 m across), piled with a sloping face toward the sea and a flatter crest about 4.5 m above the water, about 6 m wide on top, curving across the harbour mouth from the shore
objects.harbour light: a short round white-painted tower about 6 m tall on the breakwater's head with a small red lantern and a railing on top; at the quay's end a smaller green light on a white post about 4 m tall
objects.lighthouse: a round tower of white-painted masonry tapering upward, about 18 m tall to the gallery, with a few small square windows up it and a door at the base; a black-painted iron gallery with railings around the top; above it a glazed lantern about 4 m tall with diagonal glazing bars, the lens a glinting shape inside, and a red-painted domed roof topped by a ball vent and lightning rod
objects.keeper's house: a two-storey white-painted clapboard house with a red roof and a central chimney, six-pane sash windows with white trim, a small porch, standing on the rock beside the tower
objects.clapboard house: a two-storey timber house with a steep gable roof: narrow horizontal clapboard siding painted ochre, oxblood red, slate blue or off-white, white corner boards and window trims, six-pane sash windows, a front door with a small porch, a brick chimney, a granite footing
objects.sea: open sea with a long gentle swell: deep blue-green, darker toward the horizon, with a band of small wave marks that get smaller and closer together with distance; a lighter rim of foam only where water meets rock
objects.granite outcrop: rounded grey-pink granite with pale lichen patches and dark cracks along its joints, in big smooth humps and blocky ledges; grass and crowberry heath in the hollows between
objects.gull: a herring gull about 0.6 m long: white head and body, pale grey back and wings with black wing tips, yellow bill with a red spot, pink legs
objects.bridge pier: a slim reinforced concrete pier rising about 15 m from the water to the underside of the deck, rectangular in plan about 4 by 8 m with chamfered corners, on a wider pile cap just above the water line; pale grey with darker horizontal lift lines every 3 m
objects.box girder deck: a single-cell concrete box girder: the deck about 11 m wide with a cantilevered slab on each side and a plain edge upstand, the box below it deepest (about 7 m) over the pier and thinning toward the tips (about 3.5 m), its underside a smooth curve; built outward from each pier in segments about 5 m long whose joints show as faint vertical lines; the newest segments a paler grey; steel reinforcing bars stick out of the newest segment's end; no railings or lamp posts yet, only a temporary edge rail of scaffold tube
objects.form traveller: the moving formwork at the tip of each growing arm: a steel frame of yellow-painted beams standing on the last segment, about 6 m tall above the deck and reaching about 5 m beyond the tip, with steel hangers dropping to a working platform about 3.5 m under the deck with guard rails, and the formwork shell for the next segment between them
objects.tower crane: a lattice-steel tower crane beside each pier: a square mast about 2 m wide rising to about 45 m, a horizontal jib with a trolley and hook, a shorter counter-jib with concrete counterweights, a small operator's cab under the jib, warning-yellow paint; the hook hangs straight down
objects.cairn: a pile of loose grey-pink granite stones built by hand into a rough cone about 1.2 m tall and 1.5 m across at the base, the stones fist to head sized, with lichen on the older lower stones
objects.footpath: a walking path about 1 m wide worn into heath: bare peaty soil and gravel with exposed granite slabs, stone-pitched steps on the steep parts (flat stones set on edge into the slope), a drainage bar of stone across it here and there
objects.waymarker post: a squared timber post 100 by 100 mm standing about 1 m above the ground with a chamfered top and a small coloured disc with an arrow (no words)
objects.clockwork: the lens rotation clockwork: an open cast-iron frame about 1 m wide, 0.6 m deep and 1.1 m tall on four short legs bolted to the floor, painted dark green with brass trim, holding a train of meshing gears between two side plates (a large brass drum wound with a steel cable, three or four brass and iron gears of decreasing size with visible teeth, steel shafts on bearings); a speed regulator on top (a small two-bladed fan or a pair of spinning balls on arms); a square winding shaft with a removable crank handle; a vertical steel drive shaft rising from the top gear through the ceiling to the lens
objects.watch room: a round room about 4.2 m across inside and 2.7 m high: white-painted plastered masonry walls about 0.6 m thick that curve all the way round, a floor of cast-iron plates with a raised diamond pattern, two small deep-set windows, an iron ladder of eight steps up to a square hatch in the ceiling to the lantern, a curved iron stair arriving through the floor
objects.keeper's desk: a small fixed wooden desk under one window with a sloping top, a hard-backed logbook on it (blank pages), a brass oil lamp and an inkwell; a wooden chair
objects.oil can: a long-spouted brass oil can about 0.3 m tall, and a rag
objects.raised bed: a raised vegetable bed 1.2 m wide and 3 m long made of rough timber planks about 0.25 m high held at the corners by posts, full of dark soil; the beds stand in a row with paths about 0.6 m wide of gravel or grass between them
objects.seedlings: at four stages, one per bed: bare raked soil with three shallow straight sowing lines and a short stick at each end with string between; small paired seed leaves 2 to 3 cm tall in straight rows; young lettuces and beet about 15 cm tall in rows; a full crop (broad beans about 1 m tall tied to canes with string, cabbages about 0.4 m across, peas climbing twiggy sticks to about 1.6 m)
objects.cold frame: a low box about 1.2 m long, 0.6 m deep, 0.45 m high at the back and 0.35 m at the front, with brick or timber sides and a hinged glazed lid propped open on a stick, trays of seedlings inside
objects.water butt: a round dark green plastic rain barrel about 0.9 m tall with a lid and a brass tap near the bottom, standing on two bricks, fed by a downpipe
objects.wheelbarrow: a steel garden wheelbarrow: a deep pressed tray on a tubular frame with one pneumatic front wheel, two legs and two long handles with grips
objects.potting bench: a timber bench about 0.9 m high against a wall: a slatted top with a raised back board, a shelf below with stacked clay pots, a sack of compost and seed trays on top
objects.garden tools: a spade, a fork, a hoe and a rake standing in a row against a wall or a bed, with wooden handles and steel heads, a trowel and a hand fork on the bench
objects.stone wall: a garden wall about 2.7 m tall and 0.5 m thick of rough grey-pink granite in rough courses with a flat stone coping, lichen on the coping and its shaded faces, a timber gate in it; espaliered pear trees trained flat on its sunny south-facing side
objects.watering can: a galvanised steel watering can about 0.4 m tall with a long spout and a rose, and a curved handle over the top
objects.berg: a medium iceberg (a berg of glacier ice that broke off a glacier far to the north): an irregular blocky mass about 30 to 40 m above the water and about 100 m long, with steep cliffs, rounded shoulders, a few clefts, and a pale blue band or two; its sunlit faces white-cream, its shaded faces pale blue; small pieces of ice (growlers) float near it
objects.total station: a surveyor's total station: a compact yellow-and-grey instrument about 0.3 m tall with a telescope between two uprights, on a three-legged timber or aluminium tripod with steel-shod feet spread about 1 m on the ground, the instrument's top about 1.5 m above the ground; a small grey case open on the ground beside it
objects.safety boat: a small open rescue boat about 5 m long with an orange inflatable collar around a grey hull, an outboard motor at the stern and a short steering console amidships; no name or number
objects.window: a small deep-set window in the lighthouse's thick round wall: an opening 0.6 m wide and 0.6 m high (sill at 1.0 m, head at 1.6 m) in a splayed reveal about 0.6 m deep, painted white; a timber frame painted dark green with four panes (one vertical and one horizontal glazing bar); a deep sill with a few dead flies and a folded cloth
objects.garden shed: a small timber garden shed about 2.5 m wide and 2 m deep: vertical boards stained dark brown, a pitched roof of dark grey roofing felt with the ridge about 3.0 m up and eaves at 2.2 m, a plank door with a thumb latch, one small four-pane window, a zinc downpipe from its gutter into a water butt

scenes.what: the town's granite quay looking east along its edge toward the narrow harbour mouth, with the breakwater and its red light on the right, the white lighthouse on the headland beyond, and a berg standing on the open sea framed by the mouth
scenes.for: safe passage and trust (HTTPS and certificates as a guarded harbour), gatekeeping and checks, what comes in from outside, readiness and preparation, arrivals and handovers
plan: Metres: x to the right (south), y away from the camera (east, out to sea), z up from the quay top (z 0). The water is at z -2.5 at mid tide.

The quay: a straight granite quay 14 m wide from x -14 to its seaward edge at x 0, running east from behind the camera (y -10) to its end at y 95. Black bollards along the edge at x -0.6, every 5 m (y 5, 10, 15, 20 and on); a ladder recessed into the quay face at y 12; timber fenders on the face.

Fishing stores (timber sheds, ridge 5 m) stand along the quay's north side with their fronts at x -10 from y 30 to y 90; a lifebuoy on a board on the first store's front at (x -10, y 36, 1.5 m up). At the quay's end (x -1, y 94) a green light on a white post, 4 m tall.
On the quay near the camera: lobster pots stacked three high (1.2 m) in a block from x -7.6 to -6.0 and y 7.5 to 9.0; a coil of rope on the ground at (x -5.0, y 4.2); two fish tubs at (x -5.6, y 9).
The basin: open water from the quay edge (x 0) south to a rocky shore at x 140. A fishing boat lies at a mooring at about x 30 to 41, y 40 to 49.

The breakwater: a granite rubble mound, crest 4.5 m above the water (z 2), running from the basin's south shore out to its head at (x 55, y 118), where a white light tower with a red lantern stands 6 m tall (top z 8). The harbour mouth is the gap between the quay's end (x 0, y 95) and the breakwater's head.

The headland: granite rising south of the mouth to about 22 m above the sea; the lighthouse stands on its north-west shoulder at (x 165, y 285), base z 19.5, gallery z 37, lantern top z 41; the keeper's house just south-east of it (ridge at x 180, y 275, z 27). The headland meets the sea in a low granite point at about (x 175, y 330).
Out at sea: a medium berg of glacier ice centred at (x 313, y 1420), about 110 m long and 35 m above the water.
Cast: A standing on the quay at (x -3.6, y 6.4); B standing near the edge at (x -0.9, y 8.4), just in front of the bollard at y 10.

Camera: x -4.5, y -2, eye 1.3 m above the quay (3.8 m above the water), turned 15 degrees right of the quay's line (toward the basin); 35 mm lens (about 55 degrees across); no tilt; the lens shifted so the horizon sits at 46 percent.
scenes.camera: A low standing camera on the quay, eye 1.3 m above the quay top (chest height, so standing heads rise into the sky), turned 15 degrees right of the quay's line toward the basin; 35 mm lens, about 55 degrees across; no tilt. Two-point perspective with the horizon at y 497 (46 percent); the sea horizon itself sits at about y 502, just under it. The quay edge, the bollard line and the store fronts run to a vanishing point at x 466 on the horizon; lines across the quay run to a point far off-frame right (x about 7840), so they are nearly level.
scenes.composition: The quay fills the lower left: its seaward edge runs from the bottom right corner (out of frame) to the quay's end at x 556, y 522, past the bollards at x 1424, y 687 (the nearest, top), x 1057, y 614, x 893, y 581 and x 800, y 563. The fishing stores line the left edge: their fronts run from x about 110 (ridge y 265, ground y 578) to x 286 (ridge y 380), getting smaller toward the quay's end; the lifebuoy board on the nearest store at x 168, y 486. The green light post at the quay's end: x 537, top y 444. The open harbour mouth fills the centre: through it the open sea runs to the horizon, and the berg stands on it as the focal shape (x 814 to 950 at its waterline, y 502; top at x 882, y 457), framed by the green light on its left and the breakwater's red light on its right (x 1331, from the crest at y 487 to the lantern top at y 403). The headland rises from the sea at a low granite point at about x 1400, y 505, to the lighthouse rock: the tower stands at x 1474 from its base at y 392 to the gallery at y 292 and the lantern top at y 269, the keeper's house beside it (ridge x 1583, y 346), the headland's top at x 1599, y 386, running out of frame right at about y 400. The moored boat lies below the headland at the right edge (x 1797 to 1889, its wheelhouse top at y 458). The basin's water fills the lower right below the horizon. Free zones for the cast, each with open sky behind the head and the sea horizon passing behind the shoulders, never through the head: (1) A, standing on the quay left of centre, seen full length (head top x 672, y 397; feet x 672, y 784); (2) B, standing near the quay edge right of centre, seen full length (head top x 1092, y 421; feet x 1092, y 715), the bollard at y 10 just behind B's left side. Nothing tall stands behind either head: the berg is between them, below their chins.
scenes.light: Main set: a clear late-May afternoon, the sun about 40 degrees high in the south-west, behind the camera's right shoulder. Shadows on the quay fall away from the camera and to the left, toward a point on the horizon at about x -880, each about 1.2 times as long as its object is tall (a bollard's shadow about 0.6 m, crisp). The store fronts face north-west into the light at a glancing angle: lit but not bright. The lighthouse and the keeper's house are lit on their right (south-west) sides and shaded pale blue on their left; the berg's right and front faces are bright cream-white, its left faces pale blue. The sea is deep blue-green, darker toward the horizon, with small sun glints only in the right half. The sky is clear, pale near the horizon and deeper blue at the top, with a few thin high clouds. Far haze is light (the air is clean): the headland and the berg are only a little paler and bluer than the quay.
scenes.far: The sky, the open sea to the horizon with the berg, the headland with the lighthouse and the keeper's house, the breakwater with its red light, the basin's water with the moored boat, the far end of the quay with the green light post, the line of fishing stores with the lifebuoy board, and the whole quay surface (drawn complete under where the cast stands).
scenes.mid: The bollards along the quay edge, the fish tubs, and the quay face with its fenders and the ladder where they show.
scenes.near: The stack of lobster pots at the left edge, cropped by the frame (its right side at about x 140, from y 518 to y 770), and the coil of rope on the ground at the lower left (about x 303, y 906); neither crosses a cast zone.
scenes.motifs_here: the white lighthouse with its red lantern roof, grey-pink granite (the quay and the headland), a white berg on the sea, black iron bollards, stacked lobster pots and coiled rope, the deep blue-green sea

scenes.what: a single iceberg on the open sea off the headland, shown as a cutaway at the waterline: the white part above the sea and the far larger blue part below it, drawn to true proportions
scenes.for: hidden risk and hidden cost, what is visible versus what is not (culture, technical debt, unconscious bias, root causes), early warning, why a small sign matters
plan: ABSTRACT (a cutaway, not a camera view): the water below the waterline is drawn clear, as a cross-section that no camera could see, so this composition is set directly in frame terms and was not plan-checked. Everything ABOVE the waterline is a normal view from a boat at sea level; everything BELOW is a flat section through the berg's middle.
Proportions are real and fixed at one scale for the whole picture: 1 m = 5.5 px, both across and down.

The berg: a medium iceberg of glacier ice, about 30 m above the water and 80 m long at the waterline. Its keel reaches about 120 m below the water (a draft about four times its height, between the measured averages for domed and blocky bergs) and is wider than the visible part, up to about 150 m across, so the area under the waterline is about nine times the area above it (ice floats with about nine tenths of its volume under water).
The sea here is about 200 m deep: the seabed is below the frame and is not drawn.
For scale: a small inshore fishing boat (11 m long) on the surface at the left, well clear of the berg.
scenes.camera: Two views joined at the waterline. Above it: a camera at sea level looking straight out to sea, so the horizon is the waterline itself, a dead level line at y 300 (28 percent) across the frame. Below it: a flat, square-on cross-section with no perspective. No tilt, no vanishing points below the water; the scale is 5.5 px per metre throughout.
scenes.composition: The waterline is a level line at y 300 across the whole canvas. Above it, the berg's visible part is the bright shape right of centre: it meets the water from x 920 to x 1360 (80 m), rises in a rounded shoulder on the left and a steep cliff on the right to its top at x 1190, y 135 (30 m); a few small growlers float near it (x about 1420 to 1500). Far away on the horizon at the left, the headland and the white lighthouse stand tiny (x 140 to 420, the headland up to y 282, the lighthouse a white stroke with a red cap at x 300, top y 270), and nearer, the small fishing boat sits on the water at x 560 to 620 (wheelhouse top y 286), clear of the lighthouse. Below the waterline the keel spreads wider than the top: about 130 m across (x 790 to 1505) just under the surface, widest at about 150 m (x 760 to 1585) from 25 to 60 m down (y 440 to 630), then narrowing in rounded, irregular steps to a blunt keel at about x 1130, y 960 (120 m down). The focal point is the waterline where the small top meets the huge keel. Free zones: (1) the sky above the waterline from x 120 to 820, y 40 to 250, open and calm for a narrator, a mascot or a title; (2) the deep water left of the keel from x 120 to 700, y 380 to 900, calm and clear for labels and arrows; neither is crossed by the berg. The right edge beyond x 1660 is open water and sky.
scenes.light: The sun is about 40 degrees high at the upper right, off to the side, so the berg's top is lit cream-white on its right and top faces and pale blue in shade on its left. Under the water, light fades with depth: the water is clear blue-green just under the surface, deepening steadily to a deep navy blue at the bottom of the frame; a few soft light shafts slant down from the surface toward the lower left (lm-atmos, faint, fading by y 650). The keel glows pale turquoise near the surface and darkens to a deep blue-grey toward its bottom, with its lit side on the right. The sky is clear, pale at the horizon and deeper blue at the top.

scenes.mid: The iceberg as one group with two sub-groups: berg_above (everything over the waterline) and berg_below (the keel), meeting exactly on the waterline; the growlers.

scenes.what: the new concrete road bridge over the inlet north of the town, seen from a granite knoll on the hill above its south end: two piers in the water, each carrying a growing deck that reaches out both ways, and a gap of open air left between the two arms at mid-span
scenes.for: two teams building toward each other and meeting in the middle, integration and alignment between departments, a project in progress (what is done, what is left), building trust from both sides, milestones on a long programme
plan: Metres: x to the right (south, toward the town), y away from the camera (east, toward the sea), z up from the inlet's water at mid tide (z 0).

The inlet: water from the north shore at x -260 to the south shore at x 0, opening to the open sea in the east. The south bank rises from the shore as a granite bluff about 22 m high, then a heath slope up to the knoll at about 45 m. The north shore is low heath land with a few clapboard houses about (x -275, y 330); it ends in a low point east of the bridge, and beyond it the open sea runs to the horizon.

The bridge crosses the inlet north to south along the line y 150: south abutment on the bluff top at x 5 (deck level, z 22), north abutment at x -255. Two piers stand in the water at x -70 and x -190 (a 120 m main span between them), each a slim concrete pier 4 by 8 m in plan rising from a pile cap at the water to z 15.

The deck: a concrete box girder, top at z 22, about 11 m wide (y 144.5 to 155.5), about 7 m deep over each pier (underside z 15) and 3.5 m deep at the tips (underside z 18.5). It has been cast outward from each pier in 5 m segments, ten each way so far: the south arm reaches from x -20 to x -120, the north arm from x -140 to x -240. Between the arm tips at x -120 and x -140 is a 20 m gap of open air over the water at mid-span; 15 m to 25 m gaps also remain between each arm's outer tip and its abutment (cast last, after the main span is closed).

A yellow form traveller stands at each tip facing the gap (south arm tip at x -120, north arm tip at x -140), its frame rising 6 m above the deck to z 28 and its working platform hanging 3.5 m below the deck. A second traveller on each pier's outer tip.

Tower cranes: one beside each pier on the pile cap, on the east side (x -62, y 158 and x -182, y 158), masts to z 45. The south crane's jib points north over the deck toward the gap; the north crane's jib points east.

The knoll: rounded grey-pink granite with heath and crowberry at z 45, its brow (where the ground starts to fall steeply to the inlet) runs across the view 6.6 m in front of the camera. A total station on a tripod (instrument top 1.5 m) stands near the brow at the left, at about (x 50.3, y 3.2).

Cast: A and B stand side by side on the knoll top just behind the brow, 6 m in front of the camera (A at about x 52.5, y 5.8; B at about x 53.1, y 6.2, shoulder to shoulder about 0.75 m apart), looking out at the bridge.

Camera: x 55, y 0, eye 46.3 (1.3 m above the knoll), turned 40 degrees left of due east (toward the bridge's main span); 30 mm lens (about 50 degrees across); no tilt; the lens shifted so the horizon sits at 36 percent.
From up here the brow hides what is close below it: the south pier shows from about z 8 upward; the north pier, the far water and the north shore show whole.
scenes.camera: A low standing camera on a granite knoll about 45 m above the water, eye 1.3 m above the rock (so standing heads rise into the sky), turned 40 degrees left of due east; 30 mm lens, about 50 degrees across; no tilt. Horizon at y 389 (36 percent); the true sea horizon lies a hair under it at about y 397 (the camera is high). The bridge line runs across the frame, rising gently from its near south end at the right toward its far north end at the left; lines along it run to a vanishing point far off-frame left (x about -1490); lines running east along the inlet run to a point far off-frame right (x about 2690).
scenes.composition: The open sky fills the top 36 percent. Below the horizon the frame is a view down into the inlet with the half-built bridge across it, and the rounded brow of the knoll as a level line at y 794 with its lit granite and heath filling the frame below it. The bridge: the north abutment at the left edge (x 36, y 548); the north arm from x 84 (y 553) to its tip at x 506 (deck top y 597, underside y 627), its pier at x 270 from the deck (top y 625) down to the water at y 739; the GAP of open air from x 506 to x 619 at deck level (about y 600), the focal point, with the yellow travellers at the two tips facing each other (frame tops x 496, y 545 and x 631, y 555); the south arm from its tip at x 619 (y 609, underside y 640) to x 1452 (y 695, underside y 740), its pier at x 967 (deck underside y 719, the pier showing down to the brow at y 794); the south abutment on the bluff at x 1774, y 729. Tower cranes: the north crane's mast at x 358 (top y 399), its jib reaching right to x 592, y 404; the south crane's mast at x 1085 rising from behind the brow to y 402, its jib reaching left over the deck to x 789, y 417. The crane tops sit just under the horizon, so nothing pierces the sky but the cast. Beyond the bridge: the inlet's deep blue-green water, the north shore's low heath hills (a hill at about x 700, y 445) with a few clapboard houses at about x 780, y 558, ending at a low point about x 1350, y 420; right of it the open sea to the horizon, with one small white berg on it at x 1240 (y 395 to 413). The total station on its tripod near the brow at the left (x 381, from the rock at y 875 to the instrument at y 314). Free zones for the cast, each head in open sky with the sea horizon behind the chest: (1) A standing on the knoll right of centre, seen full length, facing left toward the bridge (head top x 1581, y 234; feet x 1581, y 835); (2) B standing beside A near the right edge (head top x 1832, y 234; feet x 1832, y 835). Their bodies stand over the south arm's outer end and the abutment, never over the gap or the main span.
scenes.light: Main set: a clear late-May afternoon, the sun about 40 degrees high in the south-west, directly behind the camera and a little to its right. Everything faces into the light: the bridge's near (west) faces, the piers' west faces, the cranes and the travellers are lit; the underside of the deck, the inside faces of the travellers and the east faces of the piers are in cool shade. Cast shadows fall away from the camera and a little to the left, toward x about 780 on the horizon: each pier throws its shadow onto the water just beyond it; the deck throws a long shadow band on the water behind (east of) it, broken at the gap so the gap shows as a bright strip of lit water in the shadow; the tripod's three-legged shadow falls forward onto the rock. The sea is deep blue-green, darker toward the horizon, with small glints only near the berg. Far haze is light (clean air): the north shore and the berg a little paler and bluer than the bridge. Thin high cloud at the top of the sky.
scenes.far: The sky with its thin cloud, the sea horizon and the berg, the north shore with its hills and houses, the inlet's water drawn complete under the bridge, the bridge (both piers, both arms, both abutments, the travellers) and both tower cranes, and the south bluff; then the knoll top in front of the brow, drawn complete under where the cast stands.
scenes.mid: The total station on its tripod, and the small things on the knoll: a rucksack and a rolled drawing tube on the rock beside it.
scenes.near: Only a tuft of crowberry and a lichened granite edge at the lower left corner, cropped by the frame (about x 0 to 240, below y 960); it touches no cast zone.

scenes.what: the footpath up the bare granite hill behind the town, seen from partway up its ridge: the path zigzags up to a summit cairn on the skyline, with smaller cairns marking the way, and the open sea far below on the right
scenes.for: long journeys with milestones (careers, change programmes, multi-year projects), how far we have come and what is left, pacing and checkpoints, choosing the route, a guide walking with a newcomer
plan: Metres: x to the right (east, toward the sea), y away from the camera (north, up the ridge), z up from the ground under the camera, which is about 150 m above the sea.

The hill: a bare granite ridge climbs from the camera to the summit at (-12.5, 89.1), 13.5 m higher than the camera's ground, rising about 15 percent along its crest; its sides fall at about 35 percent, the seaward (right) flank steeply down toward the coast. Rounded grey-pink granite outcrops break through crowberry and grass heath; no trees.

The path: a worn walking line about 1 m wide of bare peaty soil, gravel and granite slabs, with stone-pitched steps on the steep parts. It comes up from below the camera's left, crosses to the right past the waymarker post (2.3, 6.6), passes A's spot (2.25, 7.7), turns back left past B's spot (1.9, 11.9), then zigzags up the crest past three small cairns at (-0.9, 26.0), (-3.2, 45.9) and (-7.3, 69.6), each about 1 m tall, to the summit cairn (1.2 m tall) on the skyline.
Beyond the right flank: the open sea about 150 m below, running to the horizon, with one berg on it at about 5.3 km. The town and the lighthouse are below the flank, out of sight.
Cast: A stands on the path at (2.25, 7.7), facing up the hill; B stands a few steps further up where the path turns back, at (1.9, 11.9), looking back down at A.

Camera: x 0, y 0, eye 1.3 m above the path (so standing heads rise above the ridge into the sky), turned 12 degrees right of due north; 35 mm lens (about 55 degrees across); no tilt; horizon at 50 percent.
The terrain was modelled as a ridge (see the plan check) and every head ray was marched over it: both heads are seen against open sky.
scenes.camera: A low standing camera on the path partway up the ridge, eye 1.3 m above the ground, turned 12 degrees right of due north; 35 mm lens, about 55 degrees across; no tilt. Horizon at y 540 (50 percent); the true sea horizon lies about 8 px under it (y about 548), because the camera is 150 m above the sea. The ridge climbs toward the upper left; there are no straight man-made lines except the waymarker post, which stands vertical.
scenes.composition: The ridge fills the left half: its skyline climbs from the left edge (about y 350) to the summit cairn at x 289 (cairn top y 248, its base y 274), then falls to the right, crossing about x 568, y 379 and x 870, y 493, and dropping below the sea horizon near x 1050. Right of that, the open sea runs from the horizon (y about 548) down to the steep seaward flank, whose edge falls from about x 1060, y 563 to x 1560, y 752 and the right edge about y 800; the berg stands on the sea at x 1386, y 592. The path is the leading line: it enters at the bottom (about x 700, y 1006), runs right to A's spot (feet x 1100, y 854), turns back up-left to B's spot (feet x 870, y 666), then zigzags up the crest: x 635, y 513; the first cairn at x 500 (base y 421, top y 348); x 701, y 470; the second cairn at x 431 (y 354 to 312); x 601, y 407; the third cairn at x 361 (y 309 to 281); and on to the summit. The waymarker post stands just right of A (x 1187, from y 933 at its foot to y 667 at its top). Focal point: the summit cairn on the skyline. Free zones for the cast: (1) A on the path right of centre, seen full length (head top x 1100, y 450; feet x 1100, y 854), the head in open sky with the sea horizon about 50 px below the chin; (2) B higher up the path left of centre, seen full length (head top x 870, y 397; feet x 870, y 666), the head in open sky about 80 px above the ridge's skyline. The first cairn and the summit stay clear of both.
scenes.light: Main set: a clear late-May afternoon, the sun about 40 degrees high in the south-west, behind the camera's left shoulder. The hill faces it: the heath and the granite on the near slopes are lit warm; the seaward flank on the right falls into soft shade. Cast shadows fall away from the camera and to the right, toward a point far off-frame right on the horizon: each cairn throws a short shadow up-slope to its right, the waymarker post a thin line, the outcrops short crisp shadows. The sea is deep blue-green, darker toward the horizon, with a band of glints right of the berg. The sky is clear, pale at the horizon, deeper blue above, with a few small fair-weather clouds over the sea. Far haze: the sea and the berg a little paler and bluer than the hill.
scenes.far: The sky with its clouds, the sea to the horizon with the berg, the seaward flank, the whole ridge with its outcrops, heath and the summit cairn, the path drawn complete from the bottom edge to the summit, and the three small cairns.
scenes.mid: The waymarker post beside the path right of A, and the outcrop slabs the path crosses near B.
scenes.near: Only a tuft of grass and crowberry with a lichened granite edge at the lower left, cropped by the frame (about x 0 to 260, below y 900); it touches no cast zone.

scenes.what: the round watch room high in the lighthouse tower, where the weight-driven clockwork of meshing brass and iron gears turns the lens in the lantern above
scenes.for: systems and dependencies (every gear drives the next, and one failure stops the light), processes with a regulator, routine maintenance and checks, why a small part matters, cause and effect
plan: Metres: origin at the centre of the round room, x to the right (east), y away from the camera (north), z up from the floor. The room is a cylinder 4.2 m across inside (radius 2.1) and 2.7 m high, its walls white-painted plastered masonry about 0.6 m thick, its floor cast-iron plates with a raised diamond pattern.

Windows: two small deep-set windows, each 0.6 m wide with a sill at 1.0 m and a head at 1.6 m (four panes, a deep splayed reveal): W1 in the wall at azimuth 150 degrees (counterclockwise from +x, so toward the west-north-west, at about x -1.82, y 1.05), W2 at azimuth 30 degrees (toward the east-north-east, at about x 1.82, y 1.05). The sea shows through both.

The clockwork stands in the middle of the room under the lens: an open cast-iron frame 1.0 m wide (x -0.5 to 0.5), 0.6 m deep (y -0.2 to 0.4) and 1.1 m tall on four short legs; its speed regulator rises from the top to 1.4 m; the vertical drive shaft rises from the top gear at (0, 0.1) through the ceiling to the lens. The square winding shaft and its crank handle are on the left side plate at about (-0.5, 0.0), 0.85 m up. The large drum is at the front, low; its steel cable runs down into a round hole in the floor.
The keeper's desk: a small fixed wooden desk under W2, its top at 0.78 m from about (1.25, 0.95) to (1.6, 0.35), its chair at about (1.1, 0.55).

The iron ladder to the lantern hatch stands against the wall at about azimuth 20 degrees (x 1.97, y 0.72), mostly beyond the right edge; the curved iron stair arrives through the floor behind the camera's left (not drawn).
Cast: A stands at the clockwork's left side at (-0.95, 0.35), facing right with one hand on the crank; B stands behind the clockwork's right end at (0.8, 0.8), looking down at the gears.

Camera: x 0, y -1.95 (against the south wall), eye 1.35 m, looking due north at the far wall (one-point); 24 mm lens (about 70 degrees across, the widest that stays natural in a small round room); no tilt; the lens shifted so the horizon sits at 42 percent. The room is too small for full-length figures: the cast is seen from the knees or thighs up.
scenes.camera: A standing camera pressed against the round room's south wall, eye 1.35 m, looking straight across the room to the far wall; 24 mm lens, about 70 degrees across; no tilt. One-point perspective: horizon at y 454 (42 percent), the vanishing point at the centre, x 960. The round wall curves toward the camera on both sides, so the floor line is lowest at the frame's edges and highest at the centre (y about 911 at the far point).
scenes.composition: The clockwork is the focal shape, filling the lower middle: its front face from x 568 to 1352 with its top edge at y 649 (the back top edge at y 599, from x 668 to 1252), the gear train between its side plates, the regulator on top reaching y 420 at x 960, and the bright steel drive shaft rising from the regulator straight up out of the top of the frame at x 960. The large cable drum sits low at the front, cut by the bottom edge at about x 960, y 1080; the crank hub on the left side plate at x 608, y 805. Behind it, the white curved wall: its far point at x 960 (floor line y 911), curving toward the camera on both sides (floor line about y 945 at x 578 and x 1342). The left window W1 is a deep-set recess at the left edge (glass from about x -19 to 220, y 345 to 629), showing sea and sky; the right window W2 at the right (x 1700 to 1939, y 328 to 605) with the keeper's desk under it (top from x 1551, y 723 to x 1914, y 793) and its chair (seat about x 1563, y 947). The iron ladder's left rail shows only at the very right edge, in the overscan. The ceiling is above the frame. Free zones for the cast: (1) A at the clockwork's left, seen from the knees up, facing right, one hand on the crank (head top x 394, y 215; head centre x 394, y 287); the head is seen against plain white wall about 0.2 m right of W1's reveal (about 170 px clear of its jamb); (2) B behind the clockwork's right end, seen from the thighs up over it, looking down at the gears (head top x 1359, y 254; head centre x 1359, y 314), against plain white wall, about 340 px clear of W2. Nothing hangs on the wall behind either head.
scenes.light: Main set: late-May afternoon. The sun, about 40 degrees high in the south-west, reaches only the left window, W1, at a glancing angle: a narrow slanting shaft crosses the room in the air from the window toward the lower centre (lm-atmos, faint) and lands as a skewed bright patch on the floor at the far wall's foot just left of the clockwork (about x 470 to 600, y 930 to 990), broken by the window's single glazing bar. Everywhere else: cool, soft daylight from both windows, so the white wall glows slightly blue near the windows and greys toward the camera. The clockwork's brass gears and the shaft catch bright edge highlights on the sides toward W1 (left); the iron frame is dark green with small highlights. Its shadow falls softly toward the camera's right on the floor. The brass oil lamp on the desk is not lit.
scenes.far: The round wall with both window recesses and the sea seen through them, the floor plates drawn complete across the room, the keeper's desk and its chair, the ladder's rail at the right edge, the drive shaft, and the clockwork's back plate and rear gears.
scenes.mid: The clockwork's front: the front side plate, the drum with its cable, the front gears, the regulator, the crank handle on the left side plate; the oil can and a rag standing on the floor beside its front right leg.
scenes.near: Nothing: the camera is against the wall and both cast zones must stay clear.
scenes.motifs_here: the white-painted masonry of the lighthouse, the deep blue-green sea (through the windows), black cast iron, and the lighthouse's own clockwork (its brass and dark green iron)
details: a duty chart pinned on the wall just left of W2 (ruled lines only, no writing; it is the slot)
the long-spouted brass oil can and a folded rag at the clockwork's foot

scenes.what: the lighthouse keeper's walled kitchen garden, sheltered from the sea wind: four raised vegetable beds in a row, each at a different stage from bare sown soil to a full crop, with the lighthouse tower rising beyond the far wall
scenes.for: growth over time, habits and compounding practice, patience between effort and result, onboarding and development plans, nurturing a team, planning a season of work
plan: Metres: x to the right (east), y away from the camera (north), z up from the garden's ground. The garden is an enclosure 12 m wide (x 0 to 12) and 16 m deep (y 0 to 16, inner faces of the walls), walled on all four sides with rough grey-pink granite 2.7 m tall and 0.5 m thick, with flat stone coping; the gate is in the east wall, out of frame.

Four raised beds stand side by side, each 1.2 m wide, 3 m long and 0.25 m high, long sides running away from the camera, from y 8 to y 11: bed 1 at x 2.0 to 3.2 (bare raked soil, just sown), bed 2 at x 3.8 to 5.0 (seed leaves in rows), bed 3 at x 5.6 to 6.8 (young lettuces and beet about 15 cm), bed 4 at x 7.4 to 8.6 (full crop: broad beans about 1 m tall on canes and string, big cabbages, and peas on twiggy sticks to 1.6 m at the back, x 8.0 to 8.6, y 9.8 to 10.8). Gravel paths 0.6 m wide between the beds and a wider gravel path across the front.

Against the far (north) wall: a cold frame at x 1.0 to 2.2 (lid propped open), a potting bench at x 2.6 to 4.4 (top 0.9 m) with clay pots on its shelf, two espaliered pear trees trained flat on the wall at x 0.5 to 2.4 (up to 2.2 m), and plain lichened granite from x 4.6 to 9.4. A small timber garden shed with a pitched roof (eaves 2.2 m, ridge 3.0 m) fills the far right corner, x 9.5 to 12, front at y 13.5, a downpipe at its left front corner into a water butt at (9.2, 13.2).

Beyond the far wall: the lighthouse on its rock about 100 m away to the north-west (x -35, y 100), 6 m higher than the garden, its upper part rising above the wall; the keeper's house beside it to its right (x -28 to -20, y 92).

Cast: A stands on the front path at the gap between beds 2 and 3, at (5.3, 7.4); B stands in the path between beds 3 and 4, further in, at (7.1, 9.2). A wheelbarrow stands on the front path at (6.0, 6.5), pointing north.
Camera: x 5.3, y 0.6 (just inside the south wall), eye 1.5 m, looking due north; 35 mm lens (about 55 degrees across); no tilt; horizon at 50 percent.
scenes.camera: A standing camera just inside the garden's south wall, eye 1.5 m, looking straight up the garden to the north wall; 35 mm lens, about 55 degrees across; no tilt. One-point perspective: horizon at y 540 (50 percent), the vanishing point at x 960; the beds' long sides, the paths and the side walls all run to it; the beds' fronts, the far wall and its coping are level lines.
scenes.composition: The far wall crosses the frame as a long level band: its foot at y 720 and its coping at y 396, from the north-west corner at x 325 to the north-east corner at x 1762; the side walls run from those corners toward the camera and out of the lower corners of the frame. The four beds stand in a row across the lower middle, their front edges level at y 852 (bases at y 914) and their back edges at y 762: bed 1 at x 138 to 437, bed 2 at x 586 to 885, bed 3 at x 1035 to 1334, bed 4 at x 1483 to 1782, so the eye reads the growth from bare soil on the left to the full crop on the right. Bed 4's pea sticks reach y 520 at its back (x 1501 to 1557). Along the far wall: the espaliered pears (x 385 to 613, top y 456) over the cold frame (front x 345 to 517, y 704), the potting bench (x 628 to 849, top y 614), plain granite in the middle, the water butt (x about 1500 to 1560, top y 628) and the shed filling the far right corner from x 1560 (eaves y 440, ridge y 326 at x 1739). Above the far wall at the upper left, the lighthouse rises from behind the coping at x 212 (visible from y 395 up to the gallery at y 123 and the lantern top at y 48), the keeper's house beside it (x 288 to 450, ridge y 288). Focal point: the row of beds, read left to right. Free zones for the cast: (1) A standing on the front path between beds 2 and 3, seen full length (head top x 960, y 472; feet x 960, y 947); (2) B standing in the path between beds 3 and 4, seen full length (head top x 1346, y 486; feet x 1346, y 862). Both heads are seen against the plain granite of the far wall, below its coping (about 75 px and 90 px clear of it), clear of the espaliers, the bench, the pea sticks (155 px from B) and the shed (210 px from B).
scenes.light: Main set: a clear late-May afternoon, the sun about 40 degrees high in the south-west, behind the camera's left shoulder. The far wall's inner face looks south and is in full sun, warm grey-pink; the west wall's face (left) is in shade, and its shadow lies along the left strip of the garden about 2.3 m wide, just touching bed 1's left edge; the south wall behind the camera throws a straight shadow edge across the foreground about 2.3 m deep (from the bottom of the frame up to about y 1000). Cast shadows fall away from the camera and to the right, toward a point far off-frame right on the horizon (x about 2800): each bed throws a thin shadow along its right side, the pea sticks and bean canes throw lines of shadow up the path to their right. The lighthouse tower is lit on its left (south-west) side and pale blue in shade on its right. The sky is clear, deeper blue at the top. No artificial light.
scenes.far: The sky, the lighthouse and the keeper's house beyond the wall, the far wall with its espaliers, the cold frame, the potting bench, the shed, the water butt and downpipe, the side walls, all four beds with their plants, and the gravel paths drawn complete under where the cast stands.
scenes.mid: The wheelbarrow on the front path right of A (pointing away up the path, about x 1080 to 1280, its tray top at about y 821), clear of B's legs, and the garden tools leaning on bed 1's front corner.
scenes.near: Only a galvanised watering can on the gravel at the lower left, cropped by the frame (about x 40 to 220, y 930 to 1080); it hides no cast zone.
